title: From Cecil Scott and Smalls to the all-star Savoy band
summary: Roy describes jobs in New York with Cecil Scott, Elmer Snowden and Charlie Johnson at Smalls, and an audition band with Cozy Cole, Kirby, Teddy Wilson and Chu Berry.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But I had been to New York, see. I was in New York, and I worked with Cecil Scott first at the Les Maison(?), and from the Les Maison(?)... Did I go to the Savoy? Maybe I went to the Savoy. No, no, no. Dickie Wells got me the job down at Smalls with Elmder Snowden in '31. Then they let Snowden go, and Charlie Johnson came in, and they kept me. I was the only one he kept, you know. And I stayed there with him, and then I ended up going to the Savoy. And I was in the Savoy because they started... Oh, we made an audition for (?) City(?). It was Cozy Cole, John Kirby, Teddy Wilson, Chu Berry and myself.
Eldridge - 55
That was quite a band.
Yeah, it was. We got... Dig this. We was making like thirty-three dollars a week like (?).
[PAUSE]

We went down there and made the audition, you made; we made it downstairs first... I remember Carl Hoff. You know him, don't you? Well, he's the one who pulled my coat to it. He said, "I think you're going to get the gig." [INAUDIBLE NAME] asked me to sign the contract for a hundred and a quarter; I couldn't even spell my name! Heh-heh... Yeah, it was...

But they got rid of them right quick. So then they tried to get us to stay at the Savoy... and that's when I was offered the job to go to the Cotton Club, you know, and I said, "No-no, I want to go down there." So they couldn't do that, so they said, "Well, what about your uniform?" And I said, "Well, I paid for it." Paid for it. We paid for them ourself, you know.

So the next thing that came up was before that... Before we even opened up, Teddy had somebody subbing for us, you know, and they didn't like it. They put stink bombs in that joint -- a cocktail lounge, you know. So we tried to .........[REMAINDER OF SENTENCE INAUDIBLE]......... And like, we could work there. We could work to...
Eldridge - 56
[END OF TAPE 1, SIDE 2]
This band we're talking about... You're the leader of this band, right?
Which band is this...?
The one that you signed the contract for. The one with Teddy and Chu and...
No, I wasn't the leader.
No?

I don't know who was the leader. It was an all-star thing they got together. I don't know whether it was Teddy or who. But I wasn't the leader, no. I don't know who was the leader. But somebody got it together.
Was that the first time you and Chu...?

Oh, no, we... Oh, man, Chu... We spent many hours together with Teddy Hill, you know. In fact, when I came to New York, Chu and my brother was the first ones that really started beating me, because I was scared to play.
So this is after Teddy Hill.

Yeah. This is while we were with Teddy Hill. We left the band, put in our notice to go here. And they were trying to keep us in the band, you know what I mean. See, Kirby was coming out of Chick Webb's band, me and Chu was coming out of Teddy Hill's band, and Cozy and Teddy
Eldridge - 57
Wilson was coming out of Willie Bryant's band. You see, so we were all Savoy people, you know. So they were trying to keep us there.
